location: src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:583-596 (_gen_constant) — `name = v.get('name', 'col')` (583), `val = v.get('value', '')` (584), and the except branch `_safe_str(name)` / `_safe_str(val)` (596) which call str.replace on a possibly-None value
title: _gen_constant raises AttributeError ('NoneType' has no attribute 'replace') when a constant entry has value=None or name=None, although the executor handles both gracefully — a graph that runs in-canvas fails to save/deploy
description: When a constant `values` entry has `value` explicitly set to None, `float(None)` raises TypeError, the except branch runs `_safe_str(val)` with val=None, and `_safe_str` (line 63) executes `None.replace('\\', ...)`, crashing with AttributeError. Likewise when `name` is None, `v.get('name', 'col')` returns None (the key is present with value None, so the 'col' default is not applied), and `_safe_str(name)` crashes the same way. The exec-side `_build_constant` tolerates both: `float(None)` -> TypeError -> `data[name] = [None]` (a supported case), and a None name is falsy so `if not name: continue` skips it. Thus a constant node that executes fine in the canvas hard-crashes codegen (Save Pipeline / deploy), a worse-than-fallback hard failure on the generation path while the runtime path succeeds.
evidence: Real `_node_to_code` on config {'values':[{'name':'x','value':None}]} => `CODEGEN CRASH: AttributeError - 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'replace'`; on {'values':[{'name':None,'value':'5'}]} => same AttributeError. Executor side is pinned supported by tests/test_builder_edge_cases.py::test_none_value_kept_as_string (line 233: value=None -> [None]) and ::test_none_values_handled (line 191). `_safe_str` signature is typed (value: str) but reached with None from this path.
